page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Substitute t = log(logx)
lines: Put log(logx) = t ⇒ (1/logx)·(1/x)dx = dt, i.e. dx/(x logx) = dt
steps.why: log(logx) differentiates, by the chain rule, to exactly 1/(x logx) — so the whole denominator's first two factors collapse into dt, leaving only the [log(logx)] part to deal with.
common_mistakes: Substituting only t=logx (as in the previous few questions) and missing that this question nests one level deeper.
Losing the chain-rule factor 1/logx when differentiating log(logx).
steps.memory_tip: log(logx) differentiates by the chain rule TWICE over — once for the outer log, once for the inner — giving 1/(x logx).

steps.label: Integrate and back-substitute for the final answer
steps.why: ∫dt/t = log|t| + c, and substituting t=log(logx) back in gives the final answer nested two logs deep, matching the structure of the original question.
common_mistakes: Substituting back only one level, writing log|logx| instead of log|log(logx)|.
steps.memory_tip: The final answer nests exactly as deep as the substitution — t=log(logx) back-substitutes to log|log(logx)|, two logs deep.
